_comment: DBE Grade 12 Physical Sciences: Chemistry (P2), November 2024. The PDF has
a real text layer; questions and memo answers were extracted with pdftotext
(-layout) and read page by page against the official Marking Guidelines.
The memo is bilingual (English/Afrikaans); only the ENGLISH content is
transcribed here. Every question and sub-question is transcribed at full
fidelity; structural formulae, flow diagrams and graphs are described in
bracketed words. solution_method is the method the MEMO uses - the
matcher's content signal. Decimal commas are kept as printed (SA convention).

questions.text: The vapour pressures of different organic compounds are determined at 20 °C. The vapour pressures of compounds A, B and C are NOT shown in the table. [Table: A Pentane, molar mass 72 g·mol⁻¹, vapour pressure not shown; B 2-methylbutane, 72, not shown; C 2,2-dimethylpropane, 72, not shown; D Propanoic acid, 74, 0,32 kPa; E Butanal, 72, 12,2 kPa.] Define the term vapour pressure.
questions.memo_answer: The pressure exerted by a vapour at equilibrium with its liquid in a closed system.
questions.memo_note: Memo instruction: if any of the underlined key phrases in the correct context is omitted, deduct 1 mark.

questions.text: The vapour pressures of compounds A, B and C are given in random order below: 79 kPa, 146 kPa, 58 kPa. Write down the vapour pressure of compound C.
Fully explain your answer to QUESTION 3.2.1.
questions.memo_answer: Comparing compound C/2,2-dimethylpropane with compounds A/pentane and B/2-methylbutane: Structure - compound C is more branched than compounds A and B / shorter chain length / most compact / most spherical / smallest surface area (over which intermolecular forces act). Intermolecular forces - compound C has weaker/fewer intermolecular forces/Van der Waals forces/London forces than A and B. Energy - less energy needed to overcome or break intermolecular forces/Van der Waals forces in compound C than A and B.

questions.text: Compounds D and E are compared. Which compound has the lower boiling point?
Fully explain the difference in the vapour pressures between compounds D and E.
questions.memo_answer: Compound D/propanoic acid has hydrogen bonding (dipole-dipole and London forces) between molecules. Compound E/butanal has dipole-dipole forces (and London forces) between molecules. Intermolecular forces between molecules of compound D are stronger than intermolecular forces between molecules of compound E. More energy is needed to overcome/break intermolecular forces between molecules of compound D than in compound E. (Equivalent formulation comparing E as weaker also accepted.)

questions.text: Study the flow diagram. Reaction I is a CRACKING REACTION forming two organic compounds, W and T, as the ONLY products. [Flow diagram: Organic compound U --Reaction I--> Organic compound W + Organic compound T (C4H8). W --Reaction II--> CH3CH2CH2CH2Br. CH3CH2CH2CH2Br --Reaction III (Elimination)--> Organic compound R. Reaction IV links compound R and organic compound S; Reaction V links compound T and organic compound S.] Define the term cracking reaction.
questions.memo_answer: The chemical process/reaction in which longer chain hydrocarbon/alkane molecules are broken down to shorter (more useful) molecules.

questions.text: Write down the IUPAC name of compound T.

The reaction between pure aluminium, Aℓ(s), and EXCESS hydrochloric acid, HCℓ(aq), is used to investigate the factors that affect the rate of a reaction. The balanced equation for the reaction is: 2Aℓ(s) + 6HCℓ(aq) → 2AℓCℓ3(aq) + 3H2(g). Define the term reaction rate.
questions.memo_answer: ANY ONE: Change in concentration of products/reactants per (unit) time. Change in amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products or reactants per (unit) time. Amount/number of moles/volume/mass of products formed/reactants used per (unit) time. Rate of change in concentration/amount/number of moles/volume/mass. (2 or 0)
questions.memo_note: Memo note: give the mark for 'per unit time' only if in context of reaction rate.

questions.text: EXPERIMENT I: 1 mol·dm⁻³ HCℓ solution reacts with a 0,5 g Aℓ strip from an aluminium roll at room temperature. [Graph: volume H2 (dm³) versus time (minutes), not drawn to scale; the curve rises steeply then levels off; the time axis is marked at 5 minutes.] For the time interval t = 0 to t = 5 minutes, the average reaction rate for the formation of H2(g) is 0,033 dm³·min⁻¹. Calculate the mass of Aℓ present in the container at t = 5 minutes. Take the molar gas volume as 24,5 dm³·mol⁻¹.
Assume that the concentration of the HCℓ(aq) stays constant for the duration of the reaction. Use the collision theory to explain the change in the reaction rate from t = 0 to t = 5 minutes.
questions.memo_answer: The surface area/contact area/mass/size of aluminium decreases. Less particles exposed. Less effective collisions per unit time/second (OR lower frequency of effective collisions). Reaction rate decreases / lower reaction rate / reaction slows down.

questions.text: EXPERIMENT II: Experiment I is repeated using a 2 mol·dm⁻³ HCℓ solution. Redraw the above graph (NO numerical values need to be shown) in your ANSWER BOOK and label the curve A. On the same set of axes, draw the curve that will be obtained for Experiment II. Label this as curve B.
questions.memo_answer: [Sketch: volume of H2 (dm³) versus time; curve B starts at the origin, has a steeper gradient than curve A for the whole duration, and ends (levels off) at the same final volume as curve A.] Marking criteria: curve B starts at the origin and ends at the same point as curve A; gradient of curve B steeper for the whole duration. Note: graph not labelled: max 1/2.

questions.text: EXPERIMENT III: Experiment I is repeated using 0,5 g pure powdered Aℓ. How will the volume of H2(g) produced in Experiment III compare to that in Experiment I? Choose from GREATER THAN, LESS THAN or EQUAL TO.

Curve X is the Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution curve for a reaction under a set of reaction conditions. A change was made to one of the reaction conditions to obtain curve Y. [Graph: number of particles versus kinetic energy; curve X has a higher, earlier peak; curve Y is lower and shifted to higher kinetic energy.] What change was made to obtain curve Y?
Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 5.2.1.
questions.memo_answer: Curve Y has a peak/maximum at a higher kinetic energy / peak shifted to the right. OR The (average) kinetic energy (of the particles) increases / more particles with higher kinetic energy / larger area with higher kinetic energy.

questions.text: The reaction of carbon monoxide gas, CO(g), with oxygen gas, O2(g), is investigated. The reaction reaches equilibrium in a closed container at constant temperature T °C, according to the balanced equation: 2CO(g) + O2(g) ⇌ 2CO2(g), ΔH < 0. Changes to the conditions of equilibrium are made at different times. [Graph: concentration (mol·dm⁻³) versus time (minutes) for three gases labelled X, Y and Z, with disturbances at times t1, t2 and t3; X has the highest concentration, then Y, then Z.] Define the term chemical equilibrium.
questions.memo_answer: (The dynamic equilibrium when) the rate of the forward reaction equals the rate of the reverse reaction. (2 or 0) OR The stage in a chemical reaction when the concentrations of the reactants and products remain constant.

questions.text: Use the graph to answer: At t1, oxygen, O2(g), was added to the container. Write down the letter that represents O2(g). Choose from X, Y or Z.
At t2, the pressure is adjusted by changing the volume of the container. Was the pressure INCREASED or DECREASED?
Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 6.1.3.
questions.memo_answer: The concentrations of (all) the gases decreased. / The reverse reaction was favoured. Accept: all concentrations decreased.

questions.text: Write down the NAME or FORMULA of the gas that is represented by the letter Z.
Give a reason for the answer to QUESTION 6.1.5.
questions.memo_answer: The concentration of Z (CO) decreased with a decrease in the concentration of X (O2). OR The concentration of Z (CO) increased with an increase in the concentration of X (O2). OR Z (CO) behaves like X (O2) / follows the same trend as X (O2). OR Z (CO) and X (O2) are both reactants / Y (CO2) is the product. OR The reverse reaction is favoured to increase the number of moles.

questions.text: What change in temperature is made at t3? Choose between INCREASED or DECREASED.
Use Le Chatelier's principle to explain the answer to QUESTION 6.1.7.
questions.memo_answer: Concentration of products/Y/CO2 increases (OR concentration of reactants/Z/X/CO/O2 decreases OR the forward reaction is favoured). The forward reaction is exothermic. A decrease in temperature favours the exothermic reaction.

questions.text: Carbon monoxide gas, CO(g), reacts with water vapour, H2O(g), at T °C. The reaction reaches chemical equilibrium according to the balanced equation: CO(g) + H2O(g) ⇌ CO2(g) + H2(g). Initially, 0,6 moles of CO(g), 0,6 moles of H2O(g), 0,1 moles of carbon dioxide gas, CO2(g), and 0,1 moles of hydrogen gas, H2(g), were mixed and sealed in a 2 dm³ flask. If the equilibrium constant, Kc, for this reaction at T °C is 4, calculate the mass of CO(g) present in the flask at equilibrium.
questions.memo_working: ICE table (moles): initial CO 0,6; H2O 0,6; CO2 0,1; H2 0,1. Change: –x, –x, +x, +x (ratio 1:1:1:1). Equilibrium: 0,6–x; 0,6–x; 0,1+x; 0,1+x; divide by 2 dm³ for concentrations. Kc = [CO2][H2]/[CO][H2O]: 4 = ((0,1+x)/2)²/((0,6–x)/2)²; x = 0,37. n(CO)eq = 0,6 – 0,37 = 0,23 mol; n = m/M: 0,23 = m/28; m(CO)eq = 6,44 g. (Memo also gives full concentration-based variants with initial concentrations 0,3/0,3/0,05/0,05 mol·dm⁻³ giving x = 0,18, [CO]eq = 0,12 mol·dm⁻³, n = 0,24 mol, m = 6,72 g; range 6,44 – 6,72 g covers rounding.)

questions.text: Hydrated potassium carbonate, K2CO3·xH2O, is a WEAK BASE. A solution is prepared by dissolving some of this solid in water. Define the term weak base.
questions.memo_answer: Weak bases dissociate/ionise incompletely/partially in water to form a low concentration of hydroxide/OH⁻ ions.

The balanced equation for the reaction is: K2CO3(aq) + 2HCℓ(aq) → 2KCℓ(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(ℓ). [Titration results table, K2CO3(aq) in burette: Run 1 - volume of HCℓ(aq) used 25 cm³, initial burette reading 6,5 cm³, final burette reading p, volume of K2CO3(aq) used 20,05 cm³. Run 2 - volume of HCℓ(aq) used 25 cm³, initial burette reading q, final burette reading 48,3 cm³, volume of K2CO3(aq) used 20,15 cm³.] Determine the value of p.
Determine the value of q.
METHYL ORANGE is used as the indicator. Explain why methyl orange is the most suitable indicator for this titration by referring to the pH at the equivalence point.
questions.memo_answer: The titration's equivalence point/colour change is in a pH range less than 7 / solution is acidic / the reaction of a strong acid and weak base has its equivalence point at pH less than 7. The end point of this titration is within the pH range in which methyl orange/indicator changes colour / methyl orange changes colour at a pH less than 7.

Dilute hydrochloric acid, HCℓ(aq), reacts with magnesium, Mg(s), at 25 °C according to the following balanced equation: Mg(s) + 2HCℓ(aq) → MgCℓ2(aq) + H2(g). Use oxidation numbers for EACH of the reactants and explain why this reaction is a redox reaction.
questions.memo_answer: The oxidation number of H changes from +1 to 0 AND the oxidation number of Mg changes from 0 to +2. OR Mg⁰ → Mg²⁺ oxidation number increases; H⁺ → H2⁰ oxidation number decreases.

questions.text: Write down the FORMULA of the oxidising agent in this reaction.
It is observed that dilute hydrochloric acid does not react with copper, Cu(s), at 25 °C. Explain this observation by referring to the relative strengths of the reducing agents.
questions.memo_answer: Cu/copper is a weaker reducing agent than hydrogen/H2 (and will not reduce H⁺/hydrogen ion to H2). OR Cu/copper is too weak a reducing agent to reduce H⁺/hydrogen ion (to H2).

questions.text: Will dilute nitric acid, HNO3(aq), react with copper, Cu(s), at 25 °C? Choose from YES or NO. Explain the answer in terms of the relative strengths of the oxidising agents.
questions.memo_answer: Yes. NO3⁻/nitrate ion/nitric acid is a stronger oxidising agent than Cu²⁺/copper(II) ion (therefore Cu/copper will be oxidised to Cu²⁺/copper(II) ion).

questions.memo_working: Marking criteria: reactants, products, balancing. Ignore ⇌ and phases.

questions.memo_answer: Water/H2O is a stronger oxidising agent (than Na⁺/sodium ion) and water/H2O will be reduced. OR Na⁺/sodium ion is a weaker oxidising agent than water/H2O and water/H2O will be reduced.
